summary:
[  edit  ]
The Blend  CHOP  combines two or more CHOPs in input 2, 3 and so on, by using a set of blending channels in input 1. The blending channels cause different strengths of the CHOPs to contribute to the output of the  CHOP . It works like the  Blend SOP .
The first channel of input 2 is blended with the first channel of input 3 and input 4 and so on.
Input 1 acts as the control input, which contains the blend weight channels for the rest of the inputs. In it there is one channel for each of the blended CHOPs coming in on input 2, 3 and so on.
The first channel in input 1 is input 2's blend weight, the second channel in input 1 is the input 3's blend weight, and so on. There should be as many blend channels in input 1 as there are inputs, excluding input 1.	(However when using Differencing and Omit First Weight Channel is on, the first channel if inout 1 ias assumed to be the weight of input 3, as input 2 is the "base" and doesn't need a weight.)
The interval of the output of the  CHOP  is the interval of input 1 (the blend channels).
If input 2 onwards are just poses, it's acceptable, as the  CHOP  blends between poses by using extend conditions.
Note:  This  CHOP  is optimized and doesn't cook inputs that have zero weight.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.name: method
parameters.description: ⊞  - The blend method:

parameters.label: Proportional
parameters.name: prop
parameters.description: Each blend source contributes to the result according to its blend weight. If the blend weights do not add up to one, they are scaled so that they do.

parameters.label: Difference
parameters.name: dif
parameters.description: In this default behavior of the Blend  CHOP , the input 2 is always the "base". There are blend channels for all the other inputs, and when they are all zero, you get base. If any one blend channel is 1 and the others are zero, then your output is the same as the input that corresponds to that blend channel.

parameters.label: Quaternion (Commercial)
parameters.name: quaternion
parameters.description: The first input is used to control the proportional blending of the second two inputs using quaternions. Blending rotation channels properly involves grouping the channels into quaternion groups with the Attribute  CHOP  before using this or similar quaternion options.

parameters.label: Additive
parameters.name: additive
parameters.description: This method works the same as proportional except the blend weights are not normalized.

parameters.label: Omit First Weight  Channel
parameters.name: firstweight
parameters.description: When using the Differencing method, the weight channel for the base input has no effect, so the channel is omitted if this option is On.

parameters.label: Fix Underflows
parameters.name: underflow
parameters.description: Replace denormalized (very small) numerical values with 0. These values can otherwise cause performance issues.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: Rename from
parameters.name: commonrenamefrom
parameters.description: The channel pattern to rename. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Rename to
parameters.name: commonrenameto
parameters.description: The replacement pattern for the names. The default parameters do not rename the channels. See  Pattern Replacement .

parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

Los POPs proporcionan un sistema altamente personalizable y abierto para simulaciones de partículas, permitiendo a los usuarios definir estados iniciales, velocidades, masas y aplicar fuerzas a través de bucles de retroalimentación.6 La arquitectura de los POPs, especialmente para operadores de múltiples entradas como Attribute Combine POP, Math Combine POP, Math Mix POP, Blend POP, Merge POP y Switch POP, está diseñada para una selección, cambio de nombre y resolución de conflictos de atributos eficientes.13 Esto agiliza las tareas complejas de mezcla y manipulación de datos. El énfasis recurrente en la "aceleración por GPU" y la capacidad de manejar "millones de puntos" 4 sugiere un enfoque claro en el rendimiento. Sin embargo, la etiqueta de "Experimental" 1 y las brechas observadas en la documentación implican una compensación. Los POPs ofrecen una vía clara para

o grupos específicos deseas procesar de cada entrada. • Experimental:Attribute Convert POP: Se utiliza para transferir atributos entre diferentes "clases" (tipos) de datos, como convertir atributos de puntos a atributos de vértices o de primitivas. • Experimental:Attribute POP: Es un operador fundamental para crear nuevos atributos en puntos, vértices o primitivas, y puedes inicializarlos con valores constantes.
